items.headline: Trump rejects Iran's conditional offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz; oil spikes, reversing the weekend's talk-optimism dip
items.summary: At the UN General Assembly, Iran's FM Araghchi offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and resume talks if the US ends 'acts of aggression,' lifts the naval blockade/economic warfare, and releases frozen Iranian assets. Trump rejected the offer Monday -- 'they made a proposal but I rejected it,' saying Iran had 'overplayed its hand' -- while still expecting talks to resume this week; Brent spiked as high as $108.83 intraday before settling near $105.28, and WTI hit $96.54 intraday before settling around $92.60.
items.actionable: This failed-talks headline is the trigger for Monday's entire risk-off complex -- it reset the Hormuz war premium higher and fed straight into a hawkish-Fed/high-real-yield channel that hit equities, crypto AND the silver/gold-miner sleeve together, so don't read Monday's metals weakness as a safe-haven failure, it's a rates story downstream of this rejection.

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield hits ~5.22-5.24%, highest since 2007; 30-year highest since 2004 as Fed October hike odds top 70-75%
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield jumped roughly 6-10bp Monday to about 5.22-5.24%, its highest level since 2007, while the 30-year climbed to around 5.56%, last seen in 2004, as the Hormuz-rejection oil spike compounded an already-hawkish backdrop under Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. Rate-hike pricing now shows better than 70-75% odds of another Fed hike at the October meeting, with headline PCE tracking near 3.7% for 2026.
items.actionable: Real yields are the connective tissue behind Monday's simultaneous equity/gold/silver/crypto selloff -- with October hike odds now above 70%, Wednesday's core-PCE print and Friday's payrolls become binary catalysts for the whole book, not just the bond sleeve.

items.headline: Wall Street sells off hard: S&P -0.77% to 7,683.69, Nasdaq -0.92% to 26,820.38, Dow -0.67%, VIX spikes 8.07% to 16.07
items.summary: US equities fell across the board Monday as the failed Hormuz talks and the jump in Treasury yields to a post-2007 high weighed on risk assets; the VIX jumped 8.07% to 16.07, its sharpest one-day pop in weeks. Nvidia was a rare bright spot, rallying on new AI-safety tooling (OpenShell, Nvidia Sentry), underscoring that the broader selloff was macro-driven rather than stock-specific.
items.actionable: A broad, macro-driven risk-off day -- not an idiosyncratic tech selloff -- argues for treating Monday's weakness as a systemic rates/oil shock that likely spills into the SGX/HK open Tuesday rather than a US-only event to fade.

items.headline: Gold sinks ~3.2% to ~$4,149, silver ~4.3% to ~$61.5 as oil-driven hawkish-Fed bets overwhelm any safe-haven bid; miners fall harder
items.summary: Spot gold fell about 3.2% to roughly $4,148.69/oz and silver dropped about 4.3% to roughly $61.5/oz Monday as the oil spike from the failed Hormuz talks hardened October rate-hike odds and pushed real yields higher -- outweighing any flight-to-safety bid from the escalating Iran standoff. Silver miners fell in sympathy (Hecla down 5-6.5%, Coeur down ~6%, Silvercorp down 7.1%, Endeavour Silver down 5.9%), and no CME margin-requirement change was reported for this date, pointing to a rates-driven, cross-asset move rather than a sector-specific or forced-liquidation event.
items.actionable: This is why gold/silver fell WITH equities instead of hedging them: the channel is rising real yields (oil shock to hawkish Fed to higher 10Y/30Y), which hits non-yielding metals and levered miners especially hard -- size the silver/miner sleeve for more two-way real-yield volatility into Wednesday's PCE and Friday's payrolls rather than treating this as a clean one-way safe-haven setup.

items.headline: City Developments plunges as much as 8.2% (worst since April 2025) after unveiling S$5bn China/Japan investment push and S$6bn divestment plan
items.summary: CDL shares fell as much as 8.2% Monday after the Kwek family-controlled developer unveiled a strategic overhaul: roughly S$5bn of new investment split ~60% Singapore, ~30% China (upper-tier city residential) with the balance in Japan serviced apartments, funded partly by a S$6bn divestment programme exiting Australia (563 residential units, a 50% stake in a Melbourne office tower, a S$220m residential portfolio), selling down S$800m of UK sites, and offloading ~S$1.8bn of mature/non-core hotel assets. Reaction was mixed -- DBS's Tabitha Foo and Citi (Buy maintained) called it a clearer value-unlocking roadmap, while other investors read the added China exposure and scale of the reset negatively.
items.actionable: The selloff looks like a strategy/expectations reset rather than a fundamental guidance cut, and sell-side (DBS, Citi) stayed constructive -- worth revisiting CDL once the S$6bn divestment programme starts converting to confirmed sales rather than adding into the drop today.

items.headline: Bitcoin slips ~1.6% to around $83,000 as strong dollar, surging yields and rising oil dull demand for non-yielding assets
items.summary: Bitcoin fell from a Monday open near $84,457 to about $83,068 by mid-morning US trade, reversing Sunday's roughly flat print, as a strengthening dollar, the jump in Treasury yields to post-2007 highs, and the oil-driven inflation scare weighed on non-yielding assets including both crypto and precious metals. The move confirms crypto traded Monday's real-yields story in the same direction as gold, silver and equities rather than acting as an independent hedge.
items.actionable: Bitcoin sliding alongside gold/silver/equities is further confirmation Monday's move is one real-yields/hawkish-Fed shock rather than an asset-specific story -- the crypto book offers no diversification benefit against this particular risk today.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export-control suspension nears 10 Nov cliff; analysts flag three scenarios as $6.5tn of downstream output seen at risk
items.summary: China's 12-month suspension of its expanded October-2025 rare-earth export controls is set to expire 10 November, with analysts framing three outcomes -- a further extension, selective reinstatement targeting specific elements/end-uses, or full reimposition including extraterritorial provisions -- and little sign yet of which path Beijing will take. The IEA estimates full reimposition could put roughly $6.5tn of downstream production (autos, defense, energy) at risk globally.
items.actionable: Six weeks out from the cliff with no extension signaled yet, the structural case for the rare-earth watchlist (MP, Lynas, JL MAG) keeps building -- worth pre-positioning size/limits now rather than chasing a post-10-Nov headline spike.

items.headline: Houthis strike Saudi Aramco's Yanbu hub and a Riyadh target; six missiles intercepted
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on a target in Riyadh and Aramco facilities at the Red Sea port of Yanbu on 25 September; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted six ballistic missiles, with no confirmed damage or casualties. Aramco supplies roughly 10% of global oil demand.
items.actionable: A second, independent Saudi-infrastructure supply-risk vector alongside Hormuz reinforces that Monday's oil spike has more than one geopolitical leg -- keep the oil-shock/inflation-hedge case for the gold-silver miners in view even though Monday's price action showed the rates channel currently dominating.

items.headline: BofA Flow Show: global equity funds swing to outflow as US leads the reversal
items.summary: BofA's weekly Flow Show (week ended 23 Sep 2026) showed US equity funds losing $21.1bn and global equity funds losing a net $10.2bn -- a sharp reversal from the prior week's +$63.8bn US equity inflow (the best week in three months). Fixed income kept its 74-week inflow streak alive (+$17.3bn); the Bull & Bear Indicator eased to 9.3, still in the contrarian 'Sell' zone.
items.actionable: The pre-Monday positioning backdrop was already turning defensive before the Hormuz-rejection shock hit -- a reason to treat Monday's selloff as confirmation of a building trend rather than an isolated one-day headline event.

items.headline: Week ahead: August core PCE due Wednesday, September payrolls Friday with consensus roughly halving to ~85k
items.summary: The week of 28 Sep-2 Oct brings the Fed's preferred inflation gauge (August core PCE, running near 3.3-3.7% y/y) on Wednesday 30 Sep, ISM Manufacturing PMI Thursday, and September nonfarm payrolls Friday 2 Oct with consensus around 85k, roughly half August's 162k. Around 22 Fed speaking engagements are scheduled this week, keeping policy risk elevated after Monday's yield surge and rising October hike odds.
items.actionable: With October hike odds already above 70% after Monday, Wednesday's core-PCE and Friday's payrolls are now the key swing factors for the whole portfolio -- a hot PCE print would pressure the silver/miner sleeve further via real yields, while a soft payrolls number could unwind Monday's hawkish repricing fast.

items.headline: Mainland China reopens for a truncated 3-day week before Golden Week shutdown; HK tech heads into Tuesday's open digesting Monday's US-led risk-off
items.summary: Shanghai/Shenzhen reopened Monday 28 Sep after the Mid-Autumn Festival break but trade only Monday-Wednesday before shutting for the week-long 1-7 Oct Golden Week holiday, compressing the window for mainland-driven flow into HK-listed tech names. Monday's US-led cross-asset risk-off (S&P -0.77%, VIX +8%) and the oil-driven hawkish-Fed repricing typically spill into HSI/HSTECH trade the following session; reliable same-day closing prints for Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi were not yet verifiable ahead of Tuesday's 09:30 SGT HKEX open.
items.actionable: With only two mainland trading sessions left before Golden Week and a fresh US real-yields shock to digest, treat Tuesday's HK tech open as higher-beta than usual to Monday's move -- stay selective on 0700/0981/1810 rather than adding broad beta into the open.

note: Tue 29 Sep 2026 ~07:0x SGT pre-Asia-open run (before SGX 09:00 / HKEX 09:30).
